item.text: {"candidates":[{"draft_id":"D0041","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"MORENA's 2018 campaign pledged to eradicate political corruption 'giving institutional example' from Los Pinos (presidential palace), framing corruption as a result of a decadent regime rather than a cultural phenomenon.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"mixed","actor":"MORENA 2018 campaign","action":"pledged to eradicate corruption through institutional example","mechanism":"campaign platform; anti-corruption commitment framed as regime change","outcome":"Corruption characterized as regime product, not cultural; institutional example pledged as remedy","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"MORENA hablaba de \"erradicar\" la corrupción política \"dando ejemplo\" institucional desde Los Pinos... \"que no es un fenómeno cultural, sino el resultado de un régimen en decadencia\"","locator":"extracted HTML block 63","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"2018 campaign proposal; implementation would affect 5B.5 enforcement and 5B.7 information reliability","source_limitations":["Campaign pledge; enacted anti-corruption enforcement against politically connected actors (5B.5) requires prosecution records, audit results, and court outcomes; characterization vs. evidence need separation"],"question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","5B.10"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["The institutional-example pledge is correctly attributed to the campaign portion of block 63. However, the characterization of corruption as the product of a decadent regime — 'que no es un fenómeno cultural, sino el resultado de un régimen en decadencia' — appears in the July 1, 2018 hotel victory speech (block 64), not in the campaign platform section of block 63. The claim conflates the campaign pledge with the victory-speech framing. The excerpt as written joins the campaign pledge with a characterization that, in the source, is from a separate moment (the victory speech at the Hotel Hilton). The regime-characterization phrase appears verbatim in block 64's hotel excerpt, not in the campaign section of block 63. Split into two separate candidates or correct the attribution to the victory speech."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0042","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"MORENA's 2018 campaign characterized its platform as pragmatic social democracy accepting orthodox free-market principles, free trade, macroeconomic stability, budget discipline, peso flotation, and Banco de México autonomy, while rejecting 'neoliberalism,' privatization tendencies, and 'foreignization' of strategic sectors.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"mixed","actor":"MORENA 2018 campaign","action":"articulated platform as pragmatic social democracy accepting market orthodoxy but rejecting neoliberalism","mechanism":"campaign platform statement; ideological positioning","outcome":"Platform accepts macroeconomic fundamentals but rejects privatization and foreign investment in strategic sectors; tension between stated commitments unresolved in text","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"La plataforma lopezobradorista para el período de gobierno 2018-2024 sugería una socialdemocracia pragmática que ni comulgaba con la teoría de la lucha de clases del socialismo ni aspiraba a volver a los esquemas proteccionistas o estatistas del viejo PRI. Al contrario, asumía los principios ortodoxos del libre mercado, el libre comercio, la estabilidad macroeconómica, la disciplina presupuestaria, la flotación del peso y la autonomía del Banco de México, pero conjugadas, eso sí, con el rechazo al \"neoliberalismo\", las \"tendencias privatizadoras\" y la \"extranjerización\" de sectores estratégicos","locator":"extracted HTML block 63","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"2018 campaign platform; tension between stated commitments and 5B.3, 5B.4 implementation requires enacted evidence","source_limitations":["Platform characterization by partisan biography; actual enacted policy on fiscal rules (5B.3), competition rules (5B.4), and macroeconomic management requires separate empirical evidence; tension between stated commitments not resolved in source"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.4","5B.10"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":["Excerpt is verbatim. Claim accurately represents the source passage. Platform as pragmatic social democracy accepting market orthodoxy while rejecting neoliberalism/privatization is fully supported."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0043","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"López Obrador pledged during the 2018 campaign that he would not imprison Peña Nieto, promising 'justice without revenge or hatred' toward former presidents and their associated elites.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"mixed","actor":"López Obrador","action":"pledged not to imprison former president Peña Nieto","mechanism":"campaign statement; no-revancha commitment","outcome":"Former president and associated elites promised no prosecution for past acts; justice without vengeance pledged","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"\"No voy a meter a Peña Nieto en la cárcel\", aseguró también durante la campaña... \"hacer justicia sin venganza ni odio\"... \"no les guardamos rencor y les aseguramos que tras su posible derrota no habrá represalias, ni persecución, ni destierro para nadie\"","locator":"extracted HTML block 63","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"2018 campaign; relevant to 5B.5 anti-corruption enforcement against politically connected actors and 5B.10 legacy assessment","source_limitations":["Campaign pledge; contrast between anti-corruption rhetoric and enforcement outcomes (5B.5) requires prosecution and court records; promise of no prosecution vs. enforcement action on other actors creates attribution complexity"],"question_ids":["5B.5","5B.10"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":["Excerpt is verbatim. The no-Peña-Nieto-imprisonment pledge and 'justicia sin venganza ni odio' are both present in block 63. Claim accurately represents source content."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0044","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"MORENA's 2018 campaign proposed creating the legal mechanisms for recall of elected mandates and removal from office ('desafuero') of public officials prosecuted for corruption.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"MORENA 2018 campaign","action":"pledged to create recall and desafuero legal mechanisms for corrupt officials","mechanism":"campaign platform; proposed legislation","outcome":"Legal mechanisms for removing corrupt elected officials promised as institutional reform","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"la creación de los mecanismos legales de la revocación de los mandatos electos y el desafuero de aquellos cargos públicos procesados por corrupción","locator":"extracted HTML block 64","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"2018 campaign proposal; legislative implementation would affect 5B.5","source_limitations":["Campaign proposal; enacted legislation requires separate verification; recall and desafuero mechanisms' effectiveness in practice needs enforcement outcome data"],"question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":["Excerpt is verbatim. Claim accurately represents the source passage. Recall and desafuero mechanisms for corrupt officials correctly sourced to campaign platform."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0045","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"MORENA's 2018 campaign pledged free and open Internet access across the national territory, closure of gender inequality gaps especially in labor, and the youth employment and education program 'Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro.'","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"MORENA 2018 campaign","action":"pledged universal Internet access, gender labor equality, and youth employment/education program","mechanism":"campaign platform; social programs and infrastructure commitment","outcome":"Universal Internet, gender labor equity, and youth training-employment program promised","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"la provisión de Internet libre y gratuito en todo el territorio nacional; el cierre de las brechas de desigualdad, sobre todo en el ámbito laboral, entre hombres y mujeres; el programa de becas estudiantiles Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro","locator":"extracted HTML block 64","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"2018 campaign proposal; implementation spans 2018–2024; relevant to 5B.6, 5B.8","source_limitations":["Campaign proposal; enacted implementation and coverage data need separate verification; Internet access universalization requires infrastructure and access data; gender gap closure requires labor force data; youth program requires enrollment and employment outcome data"],"question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.10"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":["Excerpt is verbatim. Claim accurately represents the source passage. Free Internet, gender labor equality, and youth program correctly sourced to campaign platform."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0046","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"MORENA's 2018 campaign rejected the Nuevo Aeropuerto Internacional de México (NAIM) project at Texcoco, opposed due to cost overruns and environmental impact, and pledged instead to develop the Santa Lucía military airfield as the Mexico City airport solution (AISL).","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"mixed","actor":"MORENA 2018 campaign","action":"rejected NAIM Texcoco project; pledged Santa Lucía alternative","mechanism":"campaign platform; infrastructure project cancellation/replacement commitment","outcome":"NAIM rejected on cost and environmental grounds; Santa Lucía military-to-civilian conversion pledged as alternative","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"no basado en el proyecto del Nuevo Aeropuerto Internacional de México (NAIM), polémico por sus exorbitantessobre-costes y su impacto medioambientales, sino en la habilitación del Aeropuerto Internacional de Santa Lucía (AISL) a partir de unas instalaciones militares ya existentes","locator":"extracted HTML block 64","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"2018 campaign proposal; post-election decision to cancel NAIM and build Santa Lucía had significant economic implications; relevant to 5B.6 infrastructure quality","source_limitations":["Campaign proposal; NAIM cancellation decision post-election had substantial economic and legal consequences requiring separate analysis; cost comparison and infrastructure quality (5B.6) requires ex-post economic evaluation"],"question_ids":["5B.6","5B.9","5B.10"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":["The excerpt contains 'exorbitantessobre-costes' (missing space/hyphen between adjectives) and 'medioambientes' (variant form), which are transcription artifacts in the extracted block. The substantive claim — NAIM rejection on cost/environmental grounds, Santa Lucía alternative — is accurately represented from source. Minor typo in excerpt does not undermine the factual content of the claim."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0047","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"López Obrador opened his third presidential campaign on April 1, 2018 in Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua and closed it on June 27, 2018 at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, which has capacity for 87,000 spectators.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"context","actor":"López Obrador","action":"opened and closed presidential campaign","mechanism":"campaign rally; electoral mobilization","outcome":"Campaign timeline documented; June 27 closing rally at 87,000-capacity venue","dates":["April 1, 2018","June 27, 2018"],"quantities":["87,000 (Estadio Azteca capacity)"],"excerpt":"El 1 de abril de 2018 López Obrador... abrió en Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua, su tercera campaña presidencial... y el 27 de junio la cerró en un Estado Azteca, enormous cancha con capacidad para 87.000 espectadores","locator":"extracted HTML block 64","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"2018 campaign; biographical timeline marker with no direct economic governance content","source_limitations":["Campaign timeline fact; no direct economic governance content; included for completeness as campaign context"],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.10"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["Minor spelling/copy error in excerpt: 'Estado Azteca' should be 'Estadio Azteca'; 'enormous' should be 'enorme'. The dates (April 1, June 27) and 87,000 capacity are correctly sourced from block 64. These are transcription artifacts in the excerpt, not content errors in the claim itself. Recommend correction to fix spelling."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0048","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"Preliminary election results (PREP conteo rápido) published by INE on July 1, 2018 night showed López Obrador with an overwhelming, crushing victory, leading to his victory message at the MORENA election headquarters.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"context","actor":"INE","action":"published preliminary election count results","mechanism":"official electoral count; preliminary results announcement","outcome":"López Obrador declared victory; crushing margin confirmed in preliminary count","dates":["July 1, 2018"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Tras cerrarse las urnas el domingo 1 de julio, el INE publicó el conteo rápido del PREP, que no dejaba dudas sobre la magnitud de la victoria, aplastante, de López Obrador","locator":"extracted HTML block 64","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"July 1, 2018 election night; establishes electoral mandate but not economic governance content","source_limitations":["Electoral fact; economic governance implications require enacted policy evidence 2018–2024; electoral mandate does not substitute for policy outcome evidence"],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.10"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["The source says INE published the PREP conteo rápido after the polls closed on July 1 (domingo 1 de julio), not explicitly that it was published 'on the night of July 1.' The excerpt accurately represents the source content; the 'night of July 1' characterization is inferential. Claim content is supported but the temporal precision 'night' is an inference not stated in the source. Accept with minor correction noting the source only establishes the poll-closing date and INE publication, not the hour."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0049","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"In his July 1, 2018 victory message at the Hilton Hotel, López Obrador called for national reconciliation, promised to eradicate corruption — characterizing it as a product of a decadent regime, not a cultural phenomenon — and offered a relationship of friendship and cooperation with Trump based on mutual respect.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"mixed","actor":"López Obrador","action":"delivered victory speech promising reconciliation, anti-corruption, and pragmatic foreign relations","mechanism":"victory speech; political commitment","outcome":"Corruption characterized as regime product; national reconciliation and US cooperation pledged; Trump's Twitter congratulation noted","dates":["July 1, 2018"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"prometió \"erradicar\" la corrupción, \"que no es un fenómeno cultural, sino el resultado de un régimen en decadencia\", y tendió la mano a Trump, ofreciéndole \"una relación de amistad y cooperación para el desarrollo, siempre afincada en el respeto mutuo","locator":"extracted HTML block 64","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"Immediate post-election victory speech; transition period commitments relevant to 5B.5, 5B.7","source_limitations":["Victory speech contains commitments, not enacted policy; corruption eradication (5B.5) and information reliability (5B.7) require enforcement and audit evidence; characterization vs. outcome need separation"],"question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10"],"verification_status":"rejected","verification_notes":["The corruption eradication pledge with regime/decadence characterization is correctly found in block 64's hotel excerpt. However, the 'tendió la mano a Trump, ofreciéndole una relación de amistad y cooperación' passage is NOT in block 64 — it appears in block 65, the Zócalo portion. Block 65 contains the Zócalo victory speech excerpt that includes: the reconciliation offer to Trump with friendship and cooperation based on mutual respect. Block 64 contains only the hotel victory message. The excerpt as constructed joins two non-contiguous passages from two separate speeches (hotel and Zócalo) into one continuous excerpt attributed to block 64. The locator is wrong for the Trump reconciliation portion. Reject: the excerpt cannot be verified against block 64 as written, because the friendship/cooperation offer to Trump is not present in that block."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0050","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"Official final election results published by INE on July 8, 2018 showed López Obrador won the presidency with 53.19% of votes, participation of 64.4%, with Ricardo Anaya second at 22.27%, José Antonio Meade third at 16.40%, and independent Jaime Rodríguez Calderón fourth at 5.23%; López Obrador was the most voted candidate in all states except Guanajuato.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"context","actor":"INE","action":"published official final election results","mechanism":"official electoral computation; final certified results","outcome":"López Obrador elected president with 53.19% and 64.4% participation; carried all states except Guanajuato","dates":["July 8, 2018"],"quantities":["53.19% (López Obrador vote share)","64.4% (participation rate)","22.27% (Anaya vote share)","16.40% (Meade vote share)","5.23% (Rodríguez Calderón vote share)"],"excerpt":"el INE publicó los resultados finales del escrutinio, que concedían la Presidencia a López Obrador con el 53,19% de los votos, habiendo alcanzado la participación el 64,4% del censo","locator":"extracted HTML block 65","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"Electoral mandate established; transition period beginning","source_limitations":["Electoral fact; does not substitute for economic governance outcome evidence; electoral mandate strength (53.19%) provides political capital for reform but is not policy output"],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.10"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":["The excerpt as provided is a truncated version of the full passage in block 65, which also contains: 'Anaya había quedado segundo con el 22,27%, Meade tercero con el 16,40% y el independiente Jaime Rodríguez Calderón cuarto con el 5,23%. El morenista había sido el más votado en todos los estados salvo Guanajuato.' The excerpt provided only captures the first sentence. The claim is fully supported by source and all quantities are correct. The truncated excerpt is not wrong but omits supporting details that are in the source."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0051","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"On August 8, 2018 the TEPJF (Tribunal Electoral del Poder Judicial de la Federación) ruled on the validity of the entire electoral process and delivered the majority certificate to López Obrador, making his status as president-elect official.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"context","actor":"TEPJF","action":"ruled on electoral validity and delivered majority certificate to winner","mechanism":"judicial electoral review; official certification","outcome":"López Obrador's president-elect status made official by electoral tribunal","dates":["August 8, 2018"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"el 8 de agosto... el TEPJF dictaminó la validez de todo el proceso electoral y entregó la constancia de mayoría al ganador, haciéndose oficial su condición de presidente elector","locator":"extracted HTML block 65","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"Electoral certification; transition period","source_limitations":["Electoral legal fact; no economic governance content; establishes legitimacy but does not constitute economic policy output"],"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.10"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":["Excerpt is verbatim. Claim accurately represents the source passage. TEPJF electoral validation and president-elect certificate correctly sourced and dated August 8, 2018."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0052","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"In his July 1–2, 2018 victory speech at the Zócalo, López announced three basic principles: 'no mentir, no robar, no traicionar al pueblo' (not to lie, not to steal, not to betray the people), promised a harmonious and orderly transition, and pledged to give preference to the poorest and indigenous peoples of Mexico, with the motto 'Por el bien de todos, primero los pobres.'","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"mixed","actor":"López Obrador","action":"announced governing principles: no lying, no stealing, no betraying the people; promised orderly transition; pledged poverty-first priority","mechanism":"victory speech; governing principles declaration","outcome":"Three principles announced as governing commitment; poverty-first and indigenous priority stated; 'no revenge' and rule-of-law compliance pledged","dates":["July 1, 2018 / July 2, 2018 (early morning)"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"AMLO les garantizó la aplicación de \"los tres principios básicos: no mentir, no robar y no traicionar al pueblo\", anunció una \"transición con armonía\", desarrollada \"de manera ordenada, pacífica\", y prometió que los cambios iban a ser \"profundos, pero con apego al orden legal establecido\"... \"dar preferencia a los más humildes y olvidados; en especial, a los pueblos indígenas de México. Por el bien de todos, primero los pobres\"","locator":"extracted HTML block 65","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"Victory speech; transition commitments relevant to 5B.5, 5B.7, 5B.8, 5B.10","source_limitations":["Victory speech contains commitments; enacted compliance with stated principles (5B.5, 5B.7) requires enforcement and audit evidence; poverty-first distributional priority (5B.8) requires spending and outcome data; principles-as-assertion vs. demonstrated behavior need empirical separation"],"question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","5B.8","5B.10"],"verification_status":"corrected","verification_notes":["The source explicitly states this speech took place 'hasta bien entrada la madrugada del lunes 2 de julio' (well into the early morning hours of Monday July 2). The date attribution 'July 1, 2018 / July 2, 2018 (early morning)' is technically inclusive but imprecise. The speech occurred in the early morning of July 2, not on July 1. The date should be corrected to 'July 2, 2018 (early morning hours).' The excerpt content is supported by block 65 and the 'Por el bien de todos, primero los pobres' motto is present in source. Claim is otherwise accurate."],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0053","source_id":"BOOK-013","claim":"In his Zócalo victory speech, López Obrador stated that under no circumstance would the next president permit corruption or impunity, that anyone — including campaign companions, officials, friends, and family — would be punished if guilty, and that this warning was issued in advance ('sobre aviso no hay engaño').","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"mixed","actor":"López Obrador","action":"pledged universal accountability for corruption including inner circle","mechanism":"victory speech; universal no-impunity commitment","outcome":"Corruption and impunity pledges extended to inner circle; warning issued that all would be punished regardless of relationship","dates":["July 1, 2018 / July 2, 2018"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Bajo ninguna circunstancia, el próximo presidente permitirá la corrupción ni la impunidad. Sobre aviso no hay engaño: sea quien sea, será castigado. Incluyo a compañeros de lucha, funcionarios, amigos y familiares","locator":"extracted HTML block 65","attribution":"BOOK-013 (Spanish political biography, academic press)","period_fit":"Victory speech; transition commitments relevant to 5B.5 enforcement and 5B.10 legacy assessment","source_limitations":["Victory speech commitment; enacted enforcement against politically connected actors (5B.5) requires prosecution, court, and audit records; the promise vs. enforcement reality creates verification gap; contrast with D0012 (no Peña Nieto prosecution) creates internal consistency question"],"question_ids":["5B.5","5B.10"],"verification_status":"accepted","verification_notes":["Excerpt is verbatim from block 65. Claim accurately represents the source passage. The universal no-impunity warning extending to inner circle ('compañeros de lucha, funcionarios, amigos y familiares') is fully supported. Note: verification_notes indicate deterministic alignment restored the exact source substring and locator before evidence-ID generation — this verification confirms the excerpt is verbatim and the locator (block 65) is correct for the Zócalo speech."],"premium_verification_required":false}],"material_omissions":["D0050: The source in block 65 also states the second-through-fourth place vote shares (Anaya 22.27%, Meade 16.40%, Rodríguez Calderón 5.23%) and that López Obrador carried all states except Guanajuato. These details are omitted from the excerpt but present in the cited unit. The excerpt captures only the headline result."],"unresolved_gaps":[]}
